scope: Exactly these 10 #1587 tests, boundary values re-expressed relative to MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES with no other semantic change (exactly-the-cap passes, cap+1 refused, settle/release accounting unchanged): test_attachment_live_budget.py::test_exactly_the_cap_passes, ::test_an_optional_source_that_fails_does_not_consume_budget, ::test_live_charges_are_settled_once_per_key_by_the_final_charge, ::test_release_gives_a_keys_live_bytes_back; test_attachment_sources_round7.py::test_eight_million_bytes_are_within_the_cap (name kept; module gains a MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES import); test_blob_live_budget.py::test_blobs_exactly_at_the_cap_pass_and_are_attached; test_review_gaps_closed.py::test_case_attachment_blobs_served_past_the_cap_are_refused_within_a_chunk, ::test_a_counted_keys_read_draws_only_its_bytes_beyond_the_counted_size, ::test_settling_a_counted_key_again_gives_its_read_back; test_review_round12_held_str.py::test_the_second_held_body_is_refused_before_it_is_encoded (module gains a MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES import). No other test in these files changes.
reason: PR #1588 review blocker 2 (HupBaHa): url4's 8,000,000-byte decoded attachment cap encodes to 10,666,668 base64 bytes, over AIGateway's 8,388,608-byte request cap, so every call of such a run was a 413 request_too_large. The owner lowered url4's cap to 6,000,000 (4*ceil(6e6/3) = 8,000,000 encoded, 388,555 bytes left for 20 parts' padding/prefixes and the envelope) to fit that cap; these tests pinned the old 8,000,000 boundary as literals.
